Experiment – 8: Implementation of Clustering Algorithm – K-Means for Unsupervised Learning
1. Aim:
To implement the K-Means clustering algorithm for unsupervised learning using the Iris dataset, using 
Euclidean distance for cluster assignment and centroid updating for cluster formation.
2. Objectives:  Understand the concept of unsupervised learning and clustering.  Understand the working principle of the K-Means clustering algorithm.  Calculate Euclidean distance between observations and cluster centroids.  Assign observations to the nearest centroid.  Recalculate centroids using the mean of observations in each cluster.  Repeat the assignment and centroid-update process until convergence.  Visualize and interpret the resulting clusters using the Iris dataset.
3. Outcomes:
After study of this experiment, the student will be able to
 Explain the concept of unsupervised learning and clustering.  Describe the steps involved in the K-Means algorithm.  Apply Euclidean distance to assign observations to the nearest cluster.  Calculate and update cluster centroids.  Implement K-Means clustering using Python and Scikit-learn.  Visualize and interpret clusters obtained from the Iris dataset.
4. Prerequisite:
Fundamentals of Python Programming and basic knowledge of NumPy, Pandas and data visualization.
5. Requirements:
Google Colab Notebook and the Iris dataset.

Unsupervised learning is a machine learning approach in which the algorithm learns patterns or 
structures from data without using target labels during training. Clustering is an unsupervised learning 
technique that groups similar observations into clusters.
K-Means is a clustering algorithm that partitions observations into K clusters. Each cluster is 
represented by a centroid. An observation is assigned to the cluster whose centroid is nearest to the 
observation. The centroid is then recalculated as the mean of all observations assigned to that cluster. 
These steps are repeated until the centroids converge or the change in centroids becomes sufficiently 
small.
Euclidean Distance:
Euclidean distance measures the straight-line distance between an observation and a centroid. For an 
observation X = (x , x , …, x ) and centroid C = (c , c , …, c ):
d(X, C) = √[(x − c )² + (x − c )² + … + (x − c )²]
Centroid:
The centroid of a cluster is the mean position of all observations assigned to that cluster. For each 
feature, the new centroid is calculated as the average of that feature for all observations in the cluster.
K-Means Procedure:  Choose the number of clusters K. In this experiment, K = 3.  Select initial centroids.  Calculate the Euclidean distance of every observation from every centroid.  Assign each observation to the nearest centroid.  Recalculate each centroid as the mean of the observations assigned to that cluster.  Repeat the distance calculation, assignment and centroid-update steps.  Stop when the centroids converge or the change in centroid positions becomes smaller than the 
specified tolerance.

Part B: Applying K-Means to the Iris dataset
The Iris dataset contains 150 observations and four numerical attributes: Sepal Length, Sepal Width, 
Petal Length and Petal Width. The Species attribute is not used during K-Means training because the 
task is unsupervised. The known species labels may be used only after clustering for interpretation.
7. Laboratory Exercise
A. Procedure:
Laboratory exercise is based on the implementation of the above learned concepts. Students should 
follow the steps sequentially:  Open Google Colab and create a new Python notebook.  Import the required libraries: NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib and Scikit-learn.  Load the Iris dataset using Scikit-learn.  Create a DataFrame and display the first few records.  Check the dataset shape, missing values and basic statistical summary.  Select the four numerical Iris features for clustering.  Standardize the features before calculating Euclidean distances.  Set the number of clusters to K = 3.  Select the initial centroids.  Calculate Euclidean distance between each observation and each centroid.  Assign every observation to the nearest centroid.  Recalculate the centroid of each cluster using the mean of the assigned observations.  Repeat the assignment and centroid-update steps until convergence.  Display the final cluster sizes and final centroids.  Convert centroids back to original units for interpretation.  Visualize the final clusters using Petal Length and Petal Width.  Calculate the Silhouette Score as an evaluation measure.  Compare the obtained clusters with the known Iris species only for interpretation.  For each stage, display/print the required output, take necessary screenshots and write observations.
B. Expected observations:  K-Means assigns observations to the centroid with the smallest Euclidean distance.  Centroids change after observations are reassigned to clusters.  The algorithm stops when the centroids converge or the centroid movement becomes sufficiently 
small.  The final clusters can be visualized using two selected numerical attributes.  The known Iris species are not used to train the clustering model.
